sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
The green square with the white center moved 3 cells to the right again (columns 21-23 → columns 24-26). Now it's at columns 24-26, and the green with the black center is at columns 27-29, adjacent. So each RIGHT press moves the green with the white center 3 cells (one "object width" + 1?). Actually, the object is 3 wide (columns 18-20 → 21-23 → 24-26): each time it moves exactly 3 to the right, i.e., one object-width. Interesting: it's moving in 3-cell steps.
Wait, actually the object is 3x3 (rows 30-32, columns 18-20). Each RIGHT moves it 3 to the right. So it moves in object-width steps. Now it's at columns 24-26, directly adjacent to the green with the black center (columns 27-29). If I press RIGHT again, will it collide/stop, or will it push the green with the black center?
Let me think about the goal. There are two frames (charcoal 4x4 with white center): left is rows 32-36, columns 11-15; right is rows 26-30, columns 44-48. The green with the white center might be the "player" that needs to reach the frame? Or the white 2x2 at columns 30-32 touching the purple bar is a "key" that needs to be pushed into the purple bar?
Hmm. Let me think: the purple bar is a vertical wall. The white 2x2 is on its left side. The frame on the right panel is at rows 26-30. The green with the white center is currently at rows 30-32, columns 24-26.
Maybe the goal is: move the green square into the frame (like putting a ball into a hole)? The left frame is at rows 32-36, columns 11-15. The green with the white center started at rows 30-32, columns 18-20. If I press LEFT, it would move to columns 15-17, then columns 12-14... overlapping with the frame region? The frame is rows 32-36, columns 11-15. The green is rows 30-32. Hmm, row 32 overlaps with the top row of the frame.
Alternatively, the goal might be to get the green with the white center through the purple bar to the right panel, and place it into the right frame (rows 26-30, columns 44-48). The green is at rows 30-32, and the frame is at rows 26-30 — they overlap at row 30.
Or maybe the white 2x2 (columns 30-32) is a "ball" that needs to be pushed into the purple bar (like a slot), and the purple bar is a door that opens when the white ball is inside it?
This is too speculative. Let me probe: press RIGHT again to see what happens when the green with the white center collides with the green with the black center.
